topics.description: A Filipino secret society that launched the 1896 revolution against Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
aliases: Kataas-taasang, Kagalang-galangang Katipunan ng mga Anak ng Bayan

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Three Catholic priests in this country were executed following the failed Cavite Mutiny against colonial rule. A secret society in this country initiated an anti-colonial rebellion with the Cry of Pugad Lawin. A founder of that society, Andrés Bonifacio, was executed during that rebellion in this country. This country’s namesake league, founded by (*) José Rizal, spawned the revolutionary Katipunan which was led by Emilio Aguinaldo. Many revolutionaries in this country later fought against the United States which gained control over this Asian country following its victory in the Spanish-American War. For 10 points, name this island country whose capital is Manila.
parts.answer: The Philippines [or Republic of the Philippines or Republika ng Pilipinas]

topics.description: The German-born first prince of modern Bulgaria, who ruled from 1879 until his abdication in 1886.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about imported German princes who were made rulers in the Balkans:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Otto I from the House of Wittelsbach was installed as the king of this country after it won its independence. This country’s war for independence saw Edward Codrington defeat the Ottoman navy at the Battle of Navarino.
parts.answer: Kingdom of Greece [or Ellas]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] William of Wied, the new prince of Albania, quickly faced pressure from this empire to provide troops for World War I. The war was sparked by the assassination of this dual monarchy’s Archduke Franz Ferdinand by a Serb.
parts.answer: Austria-Hungary [or Austro-Hungarian Empire; prompt on Austria or Hungary]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A German prince with this name from the House of Battenberg was forced to abdicate as prince of Bulgaria just seven years after taking the throne. Troops of a different ruler with this name fought with Bulgarian volunteers against the Ottomans at the Battle of Shipka Pass.
parts.answer: Alexander [accept Alexander of Battenberg or Tsar Alexander II of Russia]

topics.description: A severe economic and political crisis in Sri Lanka that prompted mass protests, the occupation of the presidential residence, and Gotabaya Rajapaksa's resignation and flight from the country.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 2018, after a member of this country's parliament used a knife to threaten a recently  installed prime minister, the prime minister's allies wounded several MPs by throwing chili  powder. 260 people were killed in this country during three simultaneous suicide bombings on  Easter 2019. Similarly to an incident in Iraq, protestors in 2022 took over the (*) pool of this  country's president, who resigned after fleeing to Singapore during a food and energy crisis. For 10  points, name this Indian Ocean island country formerly run by Gotabaya Rajapaksa (goh-tah-BAH-yah  rah-jah-PAHK-sah).
parts.answer: Sri Lanka [Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka; or Shri Lanka Prajatantrika  Samajavadi Janarajaya; or Ilankai Jananayaka Choshalichak Kutiyarachu]

topics.description: A large, carefully constructed public bath at Mohenjo-daro that was likely used for ritual purification or other communal ceremonies.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The “Dancing Girl” statue was found at this civilization’s site of Mohenjo-daro. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Bronze Age civilization, alternatively called the Harappan Civilization, which was centered on a river in modern-day Pakistan.
parts.answer: Indus River Valley Civilization [accept Harappan Civilization before mentioned]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Mohenjo-daro was home to a “Great” one of these public locations, which was used for religious purification ceremonies and cleansing.
parts.answer: bath [accept Great Bath]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Seals from Mohenjo-daro indicate that these birds may have been first domesticated there. Male examples of these birds called roosters are used in cockfighting.
parts.answer: chicken <Ancient/Other History–Kapadia>

topics.description: Brazil’s second and last emperor, Dom Pedro II ruled from 1840 until the monarchy was overthrown in 1889 and supported Brazil during the War of the Triple Alliance.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Communities called quilombos (kee-LAHM-bohs) were occupied by people who escaped from this  institution. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this institution abolished in Brazil via the Golden Law, ending decades of forced labor.
parts.answer: slavery

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Golden Law was passed by Princess Isabel, the daughter of this Brazilian emperor who joined  Argentina and Uruguay in the War of the Triple Alliance.
parts.answer: Dom Pedro II [prompt on Pedro]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The 1835 Malê (mah-LAY) rebellion is named after the term then used in Brazil for these people.  The Spanish explorer Estevanico (est-ay-BAN-ee-koh) and the South Carolina slave Bilalia Fula (bee- LAH-lee-ah FOO-lah) were among the first of these people in North America whose names are known.
parts.answer: Muslims [or people who practice Islam]

topics.description: Julius Caesar's campaigns from 58 to 50 BCE that brought much of Gaul under Roman control and ended with the defeat of Vercingetorix.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man won the Battle of Pharsalus against the forces of Pompey the Great, securing victory in a civil war. This man captured the chief Vercingetorix at the end of the Gallic Wars, which he won. This man brought his army across the (*) Rubicon in defiance of the Senate, but was eventually assassinated on the Ides of March. For 10 points, name this Roman dictator who was stabbed by Brutus.
parts.answer: [Gaius] Julius Caesar [accept either underlined portion]

topics.description: An unidentified military casualty whose symbolic remains are memorialized as representing soldiers missing or killed in war, such as the French soldier buried beneath the Arc de Triomphe.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Twelve avenues radiate out from the Place de l'Étoile, which contains one of these structures at its center. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this kind of monumental structure exemplified by a “Triumphal” one in Paris. Paris’s La Défense district contains a “Grand” one of these structures, which evokes a giant passageway.
parts.answer: arch [accept Grand Arch or Triumphal Arch or Arc de Triomphe]

parts.label: B
parts.question: France’s “Tomb of the Unknown [type of these people]” lies directly beneath the Arch de Triomphe. The tomb is dedicated to these people whose remains have not been found after they fought and died in World War I.
parts.answer: soldier [accept Tomb of the Unknown Soldier]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This avenue radiates out from the Arch de Triomphe’s eastward face. This avenue, named for a paradise in the Greek afterlife, is the site of the annual Bastille Day parade and is known for its luxury shops.
parts.answer: Avenue des Champs-Élysées [prompt on Elysian Fields]

topics.description: The region of Gaul under Roman rule, corresponding roughly to modern France and parts of neighboring western Europe.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man reportedly died from a nosebleed on his wedding night. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this general who was known as the “Scourge of God” for his brutal battle tactics. Pope Leo I supposedly convinced this leader of the Huns not to sack rome.
parts.answer: Attila the Hun

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Attila crossed the Rhine and reached Aurelianorum in an attempt to conquer this region, though he was stopped at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains. This region corresponds roughly to modern-day France.
parts.answer: Roman Gaul

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Attila legendarily carried a weapon that was most likely referred to as “sword of the war god.” The historian Priscus referred to the weapon as the sword of this specific war god, the Roman counterpart of Ares.
parts.answer: Mars

topics.description: Red, white, black, and green are the four colors associated with pan-Arab identity and derived from flags used during the Arab Revolt of World War I.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These four colors symbolize pan-Arab identity, and can be traced to the flag used during the Arab Revolt of World War I. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name two of these four colors, which are used in the flags of Iraq, Jordan, and Sudan.
parts.answer: red, white, black, and green [accept in any order; accept any two of the four answers given]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The flag of Egypt has red, white, and black stripes and a golden one of these birds to symbolize Saladin. The “bald” one of these birds is a national symbol of the United States.
parts.answer: eagles [or a bald eagle]

parts.label: C
parts.question: By contrast, the flag of this theocratic country is mostly green, with a sword and the shahada written in white. It is north of Oman and Yemen.
parts.answer: Saudi Arabia [or Kingdom of Saudi Arabia; or Al-Mamlakah al-ʿArabīyah as-Saʿūdīyah]

topics.description: A series of coordinated suicide bombings on Easter Sunday 2019 that targeted churches and hotels in Sri Lanka and killed about 260 people.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 2018, after a member of this country's parliament used a knife to threaten a recently  installed prime minister, the prime minister's allies wounded several MPs by throwing chili  powder. 260 people were killed in this country during three simultaneous suicide bombings on  Easter 2019. Similarly to an incident in Iraq, protestors in 2022 took over the (*) pool of this  country's president, who resigned after fleeing to Singapore during a food and energy crisis. For 10  points, name this Indian Ocean island country formerly run by Gotabaya Rajapaksa (goh-tah-BAH-yah  rah-jah-PAHK-sah).
parts.answer: Sri Lanka [Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka; or Shri Lanka Prajatantrika  Samajavadi Janarajaya; or Ilankai Jananayaka Choshalichak Kutiyarachu]
